item.title: PM Tarique calls for unity of all faiths to build desired Bangladesh
item.description:
Prime Minister Tarique Rahman on Tuesday called on people of all faiths to work together to build their desired Bangladesh, saying the country belongs to Muslims, Hindus, Buddhists and Christians alike.
“Just as people of all religions united to free the country in 1971, we want to build Bangladesh together, with people of all faiths,” he said while addressing a roadside rally at Paglapir point on his way to Rangpur to visit a Durga Puja mandap on Maha Navami.
“From today, let us pledge that this country belongs to all of us — Muslims, Hindus, Buddhists and Christians. We will all work hard together to build the country into the Bangladesh we aspire to see,” the prime minister said.
Tarique said people had entrusted the BNP with the responsibility of running the country following the February 12 parliamentary election.
Since taking office, the government has been trying to stand beside people from all walks of life, he said.
As part of those efforts, the government has waived agricultural loans of up to Tk10,000 for farmers, introduced the Family Card and the Farmers’ Card program, he said.
The government has also introduced monthly allowances for imams, muezzins and religious leaders of other faiths, Tarique added.
He said the government is trying to support people in all professions and sections of society.
Referring to Durga Puja, the biggest religious festival of the Hindu community, the prime minister said he wanted people of all faiths to join hands in building the country.
Earlier, Tarique left Saidpur Airport for Rangpur by road after arriving from Dhaka by a military aircraft.
Hundreds of BNP leaders, activists and supporters lined both sides of the road, including at Taraganj and Paglapir, to greet him.
He waved back from his motorcade and briefly addressed gatherings at the two points.

item.title: Armed robbers loot 50–60 vehicles on Cox’s Bazar road
item.description:
A group of armed robbers looted passengers at gunpoint on the Eidgaon-Eidgarh-Baishari road in Cox’s Bazar in broad daylight on Monday, targeting at least 50 to 60 vehicles, mostly CNG-run auto-rickshaws and motorcycles.
The incidents took place in two phases at a spot known as Himchhari Dhala, along the hilly road through Eidgaon and Ramu upazilas. The robbers reportedly looted cash, mobile phones and other valuables from more than 100 passengers.
According to witnesses, the robberies occurred around 8am and noon and continued for approximately two and a half hours.
Victims said 10 to 12 armed, masked men intercepted vehicles, held passengers at gunpoint and dragged them into a nearby forest, where they were beaten and robbed. They said there was no police patrol in the area during the incidents.
Md Rabiul Islam, a manager at the Eidgarh branch of a non-governmental organisation, said he was travelling by motorcycle from Eidgaon Bazar to Eidgarh with a companion around noon, carrying Tk120,000.
When they reached Himchhari Dhala, 10 to 12 armed, masked men stopped their motorcycle and took them into the forest, where they were beaten. The robbers searched them and seized the cash, two mobile phones and various documents before releasing them.
Rabiul said the robbers held more than 100 passengers travelling in 50 to 60 auto-rickshaws and motorcycles hostage for nearly two hours.
Police arrived at the scene around 3pm and launched an operation but could not arrest anyone. He also said there had been no police patrol on the road during the robberies.
Abdul Hakim, an accountant at a private organisation’s Eidgarh branch, said he was travelling with two others in an auto-rickshaw from Eidgaon Bazar to Eidgarh Bazar when robbers held them at gunpoint and took them into the forest.
The robbers beat them and stole Tk150,000 and a bank cheque book, he said.
Hakim said robberies were frequent on the road and kidnappings for ransom were also common, but effective measures to ensure passengers’ safety were lacking.
Mohammad Tareq, a resident of Eidgarh who was also targeted, said he was travelling from Eidgaon to Eidgarh in a CNG-run auto-rickshaw with four other passengers around 6:30am on Monday.
When the vehicle reached Himchhari Dhala, robbers intercepted it and snatched his mobile phone. Fearing for his life, Tareq jumped from the moving auto-rickshaw and escaped.
ATM Sifatul Mazdar, officer-in-charge of Eidgaon police station, said local miscreants had set up roadblocks, looted vehicles and fled into the forest.
“Multiple police teams are conducting operations to apprehend them, though no arrests had been made as of this evening,” he said.
He added that patrols had been intensified in the dense forest areas along the 17-kilometre Eidgaon-Eidgarh-Baishari road.

item.title: Nestlé Professional signs MoU with Bangladesh Culinary Foundation
item.description:
Ahead of International Chefs Day, Nestlé Professional has joined hands with the Bangladesh Culinary Foundation (BCF) through a new Memorandum of Understanding, signed on October 18, creating a platform for stronger engagement with Bangladesh’s vibrant community of professional chefs.
The MoU was signed Sahid Sahin, president of Bangladesh Culinary Foundation, and Hosne Ara Loma, corporate affairs & HR director, on behalf of Nestlé.
Nazim Khan, Worldchefs certified master chef and adviser to BCF, chef Nayeem Ashraf joined the occasion along with other distinguished members.
Beyond celebrating the passion and craftsmanship of chefs, the collaboration represents an important step for Nestlé Professional in further strengthening its connection with Bangladesh’s Out-of-Home food service sector.
Together, Nestlé Professional and BCF look forward to creating opportunities that encourage culinary innovation, professional engagement and the continued growth of Bangladesh’s culinary industry.

item.title: 21st National Furniture Fair 2026 at ICCB on October 27
item.description:
The Bangladesh Furniture Shilpa Malik Samity (BFSMS) will hold the five-day 21st National Furniture Fair 2026 at the International Convention City Bashundhara (ICCB) in Dhaka, starting on October 27.
The fair is organized every year to promote the growth of the domestic furniture industry and expand its export markets, and it is regarded as the largest event of the country’s furniture sector.
The fair will run from Tuesday, October 27, to Saturday, October 31, across Hall 2 (Pushpoguchcho), Hall 3 (Rajdarshan) and Hall 4 (Nobaratri) of ICCB.
A total of 44 leading furniture companies will display their products and designs in 323 stalls. The organizers will brief the media on the fair at an online press conference on Monday, October 19.
Visitors will be able to see and buy the latest furniture from well-known brands including Akhtar, Hatil, Brothers, Nadia, Ayoto, Omega, JMG, Navana, Athenus, Partex, Regal and Legacy, all under one roof.
For younger visitors, a children’s art competition will be held on the opening day. Group A is open to children from pre-primary to Class 4, and Group B to those in Classes 5 to 8.
Registration begins at 2:00 PM and the competition starts at 4:00 PM.
Twenty children will receive awards, with total prize money of about Tk200,000.
Speaking about the fair, Sheikh Abdul Awal, convener of the organizing committee and vice chairman of BFSMS: said, "This fair is entirely focused on domestic consumers. Only locally made furniture will be on display, and there will be no imported furniture. The participating companies are coming with new designs, and this is a great opportunity for furniture manufacturers to show the country their latest design innovations. To boost sales, visitors will get discounts of up to 15 percent."
The opening ceremony will begin at 10:30 AM on Tuesday, October 27, in Hall 4 (Nobaratri).
Mohammad Hasan Arif, vice chairman and chief executive officer of the Export Promotion Bureau (EPB), will attend as chief guest.
Md Fazlul Haque, administrator of FBCCI, and KM Akhtaruzzaman, president of the Bangladesh Furniture Exporters Association, will attend as special guests.
The ceremony will be chaired by Selim H Rahman, chairman of BFSMS.
Md Elias Sarker, senior vice chairman, A Karim Mazumder, secretary general, and Mohammad Maksudur Rahman, organizing secretary of BFSMS, will also speak.
The fair will be open to visitors every day from October 27-31, from 10:00 AM to 9:00 PM, at ICCB.
Entry is free and no ticket is required.
The media partners of the fair are ATN Bangla, Kalbela and Access Infotech.

item.title: Teenager’s body recovered from pond near PM Tarique’s rally venue
item.description:
Police recovered the semi-decomposed body of an 18-year-old, Rafsan bin Abdullah, from a pond in Rajshahi on Tuesday morning, about half a kilometre from the historic Madrasa Ground, where Prime Minister Tarique Rahman is scheduled to address a public rally.
Rafsan had been missing since leaving home on Monday morning. His body was found floating in a pond south of the Shah Makhdum Institute Public Library around 9am on Tuesday.
Tarique is scheduled to attend the rally, organised by the BNP’s city and district units, as the chief guest at Madrasa Ground at 3pm.
Deputy Commissioner Gaziur Rahman, spokesperson for Rajshahi Metropolitan Police (RMP), said Rafsan lived in the city’s Hosseiniganj Betpatti area. His father is Abdullah Zaki Rubel.
He said an initial examination found no visible signs of injury on the body. Rafsan was wearing shorts but no shirt, and the body had begun to decompose.
The body was sent to the morgue at Rajshahi Medical College Hospital for an autopsy.
Police said their preliminary assessment suggested that Rafsan might have drowned after entering the pond to bathe. His family said he did not know how to swim.
However, the exact cause of death will be determined after the autopsy report is received, police said.

item.title: Unicef chief calls for investment in children, action to end child marriage
item.description:
Unicef Executive Director Catherine Russell has called for urgent investment in children in Bangladesh following a three-day visit that included meetings with families in Korail, Dhaka’s largest informal settlement, and Rohingya refugees and host communities in Cox’s Bazar.
Russell urged action on three fronts: ending child marriage and keeping girls in school; fulfilling the government’s commitment to invest 5% of gross domestic product (GDP) in education and health; and protecting access to quality education for Rohingya and host-community children.
In Korail, Russell heard from children and parents about poverty, disrupted education and limited access to basic services. Adolescent girls shared their ambitions and the pressures that can force them to leave school and marry.
“I met a 14-year-old girl named Bushra, who told me how community leaders at a Unicef-supported child protection hub had worked with Bushra’s father to save her from early marriage,” Russell said.
“Keeping girls in school and providing them with the health, education and protection services they need will deliver a brighter future for them, for their communities, and for Bangladesh.”
Nearly half, or 47.2%, of women aged 20-24 in Bangladesh were married before the age of 18, according to the Bangladesh Multiple Indicator Cluster Survey 2025.
Child marriage pushes girls out of school, fuels early pregnancy and limits their opportunities throughout life. Unicef has called for girls to complete secondary education and for loopholes in national law that permit child marriage to be addressed.
Russell met senior officials, including Shama Obaed Islam, state minister for foreign affairs. She expressed appreciation for the government’s commitment to increasing the budgets for education and health services, stressing the importance of turning pledges into action.
“Budgets reflect priorities,” Russell said. “Investing in children’s quality education, health, nutrition and protection is investing in Bangladesh’s future.”
In Cox’s Bazar, home to one of the world’s largest refugee camps, Russell met Rohingya children and families and visited Unicef-supported learning activities.
Recognising Bangladesh’s generosity in hosting Rohingya refugees, Russell urged the international community to continue supporting both refugees and host communities.
At a Unicef-supported learning centre, she heard from students and teachers about the importance of education and vocational skills. Beyond learning, education helps protect children from exploitation, trafficking, child marriage and recruitment by armed groups.
“Rohingya children have lost so much to violence, displacement and uncertainty. They cannot lose their education too,” Russell said. “The world must invest in them, and in the communities that welcomed them.”
Across Bangladesh, Unicef works with the government and partners to strengthen the systems and services on which children and families depend. Its support includes access to quality education, primary health care, immunisation, nutrition, safe water, sanitation and child protection services.
Unicef also works to prevent child marriage and violence against children, empower adolescent girls, strengthen social protection and promote greater public investment in children. Through research, policy advocacy and support for national and local institutions, it seeks to ensure essential services reach children most at risk of being left behind.
In Cox’s Bazar, Unicef and its partners provide life-saving and essential services to Rohingya refugee children and families, including malnutrition prevention and treatment, safe drinking water, sanitation, education, health care, child protection and psychosocial support. The organisation also supports vulnerable host communities.
As humanitarian funding declines, sustained international support is critical to protecting essential services, preserving progress and ensuring that refugee and host-community children are not left behind.

item.title: PM leaves Dhaka to visit Durga Puja mandaps in 3 districts
item.description:
Prime Minister Tarique Rahman left Dhaka for Rangpur on Tuesday morning to visit Durga Puja mandaps outside the capital on Maha Navami, the ninth day of the Hindu community’s Sharadiya festival.
He left Tejgaon Airport at 9am by a military aircraft, Prime Minister’s Press Secretary Saleh Shibly told UNB.
“The prime minister has left for Rangpur. He will visit the puja mandap at Radha Gobinda Temple and exchange greetings with devotees there,” he said.
Tarique is scheduled to visit puja mandaps in Rangpur, Rajshahi and Chittagong districts before returning to Dhaka at night, Shibly said.
He said the government has taken all necessary measures to ensure the smooth celebration of Durga Puja across the country.
“The government’s policy is that religion belongs to each individual, but everyone has the right to security. The allocation has been increased, holidays have been extended, and all kinds of support are being provided to puja mandaps,” the press secretary said.
A number of senior BNP leaders and government officials are accompanying the Prime Minister, including BNP Standing Committee member Gayeshwar Chandra Roy, Women and Children Affairs Minister Prof AZM Zahid Hussain, BNP Acting Secretary General Ruhul Kabir Rizvi, Culture Minister Nitai Roy Chowdhury and State Minister for Local Government Mir Shah Alam.
Others in the entourage include Prime Minister’s Adviser Rehan Asif Asad, Special Assistant Bijon Kanti Sarkar, BNP Special Secretary Belayet Hossain Mridha, Hindu Religious Welfare Trust Vice-Chairman and MP Nipun Roy Chowdhury, BNP Assistant Organising Secretary Jayanta Kumar Kundu, Press Secretary Saleh Shibly and Additional Press Secretary Atikur Rahman Rumon.
According to the itinerary, Tarique will travel from Saidpur Airport to Rangpur’s Radha Gobinda Temple after arriving in Saidpur at 10am.
He is scheduled to leave Saidpur for Rajshahi at 12:30pm and visit the Dharmasabha Temple’s puja mandap at around 1:15pm.
After a brief stop at Rajshahi Circuit House, he will attend a public rally at Haji Muhammad Mohsin Government High School ground at 3pm.
The prime minister will then fly to Chittagong, where he is scheduled to visit the puja mandap at JM Sen Hall in Rahmatganj at 5:30pm. After a brief stop at Chittagong Circuit House, he is scheduled to leave Shah Amanat International Airport for Dhaka at 7:45pm and arrive at Tejgaon Airport at 9:15pm.

item.title: Ronaldo handed 30-day suspension after walking out on Portugal
item.description:
Cristiano Ronaldo has been handed a 30-day suspension for leaving the Portuguese national team camp, the country's football federation (FPF) announced on Monday.
The 41-year-old abruptly left the Portugal camp on September 30 during the UEFA Nations League, before accusing coach Jorge Jesus of breaking his word about giving him game time.
Ronaldo apologised to supporters earlier in October, adding he would accept any punishment that was imposed.
The former Manchester United and Real Madrid star, who will also have to pay a fine of 255 euros ($286), has received the minimum penalty provided for in the federation's regulations, which stipulate suspensions of between one and six months for leaving the national team.
Ronaldo left Portugal's squad after first being made to warm up as a substitute against Norway on September 27 and not being brought on, and then finding out he would not start against Denmark in the match on October 1.
Ronaldo's suspension takes effect from the day of the Denmark match, meaning he has already served 19 days of his ban and will complete it by the end of October.
The FPF disciplinary committee said it took into account "the remorse shown in the statement" issued by Ronaldo on October 6, in which he admitted his mistake and expressed his willingness to accept a punishment.
The five-time Ballon d'Or winner is Portugal's all-time top goalscorer and record appearance-maker in men's international football.
But in his absence, Portugal won all four of their Nations League matches and qualified for the quarter-finals with two games to spare.
Portugal host Denmark on November 14 and then travel to face Wales on November 17 in their final two Nations League Group A4 matches -- by which time Ronaldo will have served his suspension.
In a social media post shortly after his walk-out, Ronaldo accused Portugal boss Jesus of breaking his word about giving him game time in Nations League matches but insisted he was not retiring from international duty.
"I will be available, as I have always been until today, to compete and win for our national team," Ronaldo posted.
He said Jesus had gone back on his word about bringing him on against Norway, and then in a press conference before the Denmark match had not said a series of points they had agreed upon during a conversation beforehand.
One of Ronaldo's pre-approved talking points was that Jesus had "made a mistake in asking someone of the stature of Pele or Maradona to warm up and then not sending him on in the match".
Jesus, speaking several days later, said he would select Ronaldo for international duty if the forward was playing for his club Al Nassr, and was interested in being called up.
Following the FPF's announcement, Ronaldo did not directly react to the news on Instagram but did post a picture of himself preparing to train with his Saudi club, accompanied with the caption, "Putting in the work".

item.title: Real Madrid's rough Diomande starting to shine as Leipzig visit
item.description:
When Real Madrid splashed a club record 140 million euros ($157m) to sign Yan Diomande from RB Leipzig this summer, it was because of his clear potential to become one of the game's stars, as showcased at the 2026 World Cup.
That talent has begun to unveil itself in recent matches, with Diomande lashing in a spectacular strike against Sevilla on Sunday in La Liga ahead of a reencounter with his former side Leipzig in the Champions League on Wednesday.
Diomande's sheer potential was not, however, the only reason Madrid forked out.
President Florentino Perez pledged to fans during his campaign for reelection in June that he would pay a fee of that magnitude for a new star as Madrid tried to rebuild following two seasons without a major trophy.
Diomande had demonstrated exciting promise, shining with Leipzig during just one season in Germany after emerging at Spanish side Leganes.
The 19-year-old did not join Madrid to fill an obvious vacancy, with his arrival actually exacerbating an overbooking in attack.
On the same day Diomande's transfer was announced, Brazilian winger Vinicius Junior signed a new deal until 2032 with Los Blancos.
Madrid struggled last season to find a balance with Kylian Mbappe, Jude Bellingham and Vinicius on the pitch together, let alone throwing a new attacking star carrying a record price tag into the mix.
For a combination of those factors, it should not come as a surprise that Diomande is still finding his footing in the Spanish capital.
The youngster has shown flashes of his great quality, without yet firmly establishing himself as an essential figure for coach Jose Mourinho, although he is improving.
Diomande scored his first goal for the club against Villarreal on October 10, securing Real Madrid a 1-0 win.
The winger's superb finish was not the main talking point though, after Vinicius was dismissed later in the game and subsequently banned for four matches.
That further opened the door for Diomande to settle in, with the winger starting on the left wing in Sunday's 4-1 rout of Sevilla, in which he lashed home from long range in the final stages.
Diomande also assisted the opener for Arda Guler, in his best performance for the club thus far. In total he has two goals and three assists in 11 appearances across all competitions.
"He has a lot to improve, he's young, he's still naive, he's still not the finished article," said Mourinho on Sunday.
"At Real Madrid, the demands are very high... but he had a great game, he's growing."
- 'I will die trying' -
Diamonds form under pressure, and thus far in his career Diomande has handled it on and off the pitch.
He suffered rejection after leaving the Ivory Coast to go to school in Florida in the United States, unable to reach a deal with MLS sides Charlotte FC and Colorado Rapids.
Eventually the winger's senior debut came with Leganes against Real Madrid in March 2025, and in 10 games for the club he netted twice, earning himself a move to Germany.
Diomande helped Leipzig reach the Champions League with 12 goals and eight assists, and he was named "rookie of the year" in the Bundesliga, before his Madrid move.
The winger said he is spurred on by tragedy from his life. His sister Roxane died at age 15 in 2025 after her drink was spiked, Diomande explained in an open letter, published by The Player's Tribune in June.
"You were the one who always believed that I could be the next Cristiano (Ronaldo), when everybody else laughed," wrote Diomande to his late sister.
"You were telling everybody, 'My brother is going to be the greatest in the world'. I will prove that you were right, or I will die trying."
At the home of the record 15-time European champions, Diomande has the platform to do that.
"He has to improve his finishing... assist better... but that will come," added Mourinho.
"I remember when Vinicius arrived (and struggled), and in two or three years Vinicius was a top drawer player."
Vinicius is not suspended in Europe put Diomande will be hoping Mourinho gives him another chance to shine against his former side Leipzig on Wednesday, as Madrid aim for a third win from three Champions League games.

item.title: The price of buying small
item.description:
“We are struggling.” “I can’t feed my family.” “ It’s getting really tough to get by.”
At first glance, these testimonies might seem to reflect quotes of an economy in depression or communities enduring the upheaval of war. However, they are the mundane realities of working-class households in Bangladesh - - a country neither at war nor in severe distress. Yet, the world seems to be maliciously devised in ways that consistently leave them at the short end of the stick.
The economic realities of Bangladesh - - institutional shortcomings coupled with rising inflation - - have left nearly 28% of people in poverty, according to a 2025 PPRC survey. For the sake of simplicity, poverty is often reduced to the notion of having limited financial means. But what if poverty is not just about having less money? What if, in the very act of struggling to make ends meet, the poor are made to pay relatively more for the same necessities that the wealthy can afford for less?
Oscar Lewis’s culture of poverty theorizes that poverty is a self-perpetuating cycle through attitudes, behaviour and values that emerge under conditions of persistent deprivation. However, the cycle of entrapment occurs in more insidious ways, specifically through concepts like poverty premium. Consider a kilogram of sugar - in retail, it costs around ৳ 110/kg; but in bulk, it is only ৳ 90/kg -- a 19% decrease.
Sugar is hardly an isolated case. We have found larger disparities across several essential goods. Masoor dal , for instance, showed a price difference of 45% between retail and bulk purchasing, while onion showed a gap of 44%. Rice, perhaps the most important staple product in our households, was around 36% cheaper when purchased in bulk. Atta and m aid a have shown similar differences, at roughly 37% and 34% respectively. Each of these comparisons is like for like: T he same product, of the same quality, priced on the same day. The only thing that changed was how much was bought.
a typical 4.26-person household, rice alone accounts for 42 kilograms of consumption monthly. Because of this sheer volume, even a modest price difference across several retail purchases can aggregate to a substantial monthly expense. In our household basket calculation, rice itself accounted for roughly Tk 1,303 of the Tk 1,815 in potential monthly savings, approximately 72% of the total.
Across the basket, the difference between retail and bulk purchasing amounted to Tk 1,815 per month for a household eating at national average levels, or Tk 21,780 per year. Among Bangladesh’s poorest households, whose monthly expenditure exceeds income by roughly Tk 3,817, the potential savings would represent nearly half of that deficit. While the numbers are staggering, they barely capture the harshness of reality : I f the poorest households live on about Tk 283 a day, how can they afford any bulk products? If they can’t do so individually, could they access them collectively?
This is the idea behind Shomobay . Within neighbourhoods , families pre-register their weekly requirements. Afterwards, their demands are aggregated. We buy in bulk from the nearest wholesaler and hand everything over the same day at a collection point, at close to the bulk price -- curbing any storage constraints. The family does not have to become a bulk buyer. Instead, Shomobay becomes the intermediary between all the customers of bulk products in the neighbourhood , establishing a collective initiative.
The aim is not to reinvent how groceries are bought, but to recalibrate the purchasing position of the household; and that is what Shomobay achieved in the first pilot.
Anwar, one of the participants in the pilot, stated, “If I could buy through Shomobay every week, my monthly savings would increase significantly.” Fatema, a mother of three, echoed the same sense of optimism, “Because of this initiative, after buying the household groceries, I still have enough money left to buy other things.” If each of the 15 pilot families bought the full basket this way every month, they would collectively save about ৳ 27,225 a month. Across 1,000 families, that becomes about ৳ 18 lakh a month, or more than ৳ 2 crore a year. For a single family, the saving is about twice what a year of food inflation adds to a family’s grocery bill. Over a year, it adds up to roughly 45 days of wages for a garment worker on minimum wage. Broken down to a single day, the saving comes to about ৳ 60. In the poorest tenth of households, that is close to what one person lives on in a day.
Bangladesh is not short of attempts to make groceries cheaper. While TCB provides subsidized lentils, oils and sugar, coverage has shrunk from 1 crore families to roughly 70 lakh after mass cancellations. Truck sales arrive irregularly, often with long queues. Buyers we spoke to also raised concerns of corruption, syndicates and poor quality. Additionally, newer state initiatives like the Family Card are barely accessible to the people who need it most.
Abroad, the idea of pooling demand has been tried at scale. India’s DealShare was once valued at $1.7 billion; by 2026, it was in sale talks worth around $90 million. Kenya’s Twiga Foods, which raised over $150 million, entered administration in August 2026. China’s community group buying startups ended in a price war. Each time, the model has broken down the same way: prices subsidized with investor money, expensive warehouses and delivery fleets, or credit that customers could not repay.
Shomobay is built to avoid all three. There is no subsidy, families pay the real bulk price. No warehouse, goods are bought and sold upfront. No credit, families pay upfront. Shomobay does not aim to replace TCB but rather to mitigate the shortcomings that it has been plagued with for years.
As we continue refining the model, Shomobay is building a wider presence beyond the neighbourhoods in which it operates. We envision Shomobay growing from neighbourhoods to cities, from cities to communities across Bangladesh, and eventually beyond Bangladesh, wherever households face the same fundamental disadvantage of paying more simply because they can afford to buy less.
Jaif Bin Morshed is a r esearch i ntern, PRI (Policy Research Institute) .

Durga Puja: Maha Nabami celebrated, Bijaya Dashami tomorrow
item.description:
Maha Nabami of the Sharadiya Durga Puja was celebrated across the country with due religious fervour and gaiety while the devotees are waiting for celebrating the Bijaya Dashami tomorrow, Wednesday.

Bijaya Dashami will be celebrated tomorrow bidding farewell to Goddess Durga as devotees will take the idols in processions to designated rivers, ponds and other water bodies for immersion, known as ‘Bisarjan or Niranjan’.

Marking the Maha Nabami, Various rituals including NabamiBihit puja, Boli (sacrificing of animals or vegetables like pumpkin, sugarcane and banana), offering of ‘bhog and pushpanjali, home joggo, distribution of Charanamrito and “Maha Prashad” were held this morning at mandaps.
Devotees offered ‘Anjali’ after keeping fasting as major concluding worship rituals marking the day.

Puja mandaps across the country have been engaged with devotees and visitors since last Friday when the six-day festival began with the ceremonial invocation of Goddess Durga on Maha Shashthi.

Vibrant decorations, traditional ‘dhak’ beats, the ringing of ‘kashor and ghonta’, ‘conch-shell blasts and ‘ululation’ have added to the festive atmosphere.

Devotees have been visiting puja pandals across the country to offer prayers and enjoy the celebrations.

A total of 33,851 puja mandaps have been set up across the country this year, including 258 in the capital, according to the Bangladesh Puja Udjapan Parishad. The number has increased by nearly 1,500 compared to the last year.

The Gulshan-Banani Puja Foundation is hosting one of the most elaborate celebrations at Kamal Ataturk Park in Banani.

Makeshift pandals at Kalabagan ground and Khamarbari have also emerged as major attractions for visitors in the capital, with large structures and eye-catching lighting displays drawing crowds.

In the capital, a large number of Durga Puja celebrations are being held in the old parts of the city, including Tantibazar and Shakharibazar.

Ramna Kali Mandir, Siddheshwari Kali Mandir, Dhaka University's Jagannath Hall and Uttara Sarbajanin Mandir are also witnessing large numbers of visitors every day during the festival.

item.title: Additional DIG relieved of duties after police detain 85 in raid on his house
item.description:
Additional Deputy Inspector General of Police Abdullah Al Zahir has been relieved of his duties after police raided a house owned by him in the Vatara police station area of the capital, seized various drugs and detained 85 people.

Abdullah Al Zahir was working in the Maintenance and Repair section of Police Headquarters. He has been withdrawn from that post and attached to Police Headquarters.

The information was announced in an office order signed by Mohammad Sharif Uddin, additional DIG (Confidential) at Police Headquarters, on Tuesday afternoon.

Earlier, around midnight on Monday, a team from the Detective Branch’s Uttara division raided the three-storey house in the Police Housing-1 residential area.

The DB said illegal drug use and a DJ party were taking place there. According to DB sources, police seized cannabis, yaba tablets, alcohol and equipment used to consume yaba during the raid.

Additional Commissioner (DB) of Dhaka Metropolitan Police Shafiqul Islam said the additional DIG had rented out the house through an online platform. The tenants had been using the property for drug-related activities, he added.

Of the 85 people detained, 26 are women. The detainees will be tried and punished through the legal process, Shafiqul Islam said.

item.title: Clear intelligence indicates two sides have joined hands, says PM
item.description:
Prime Minister Tarique Rahman has said attempts have been made to foment labour unrest at several locations and industrial establishments across the country. He said intelligence agencies have clear information that the fugitive autocrat is providing funds to stir up labour unrest. Several political parties that tried to sell different kinds of tickets to the public ahead of the election have also joined the effort, he added.

The prime minister made the remarks at a rally at Madrasa Ground in Rajshahi on Tuesday afternoon.

Referring to the activities-banned Awami League and the opposition Bangladesh Jamaat-e-Islami in connection with the labour unrest, Tarique Rahman said, “We have clear intelligence that the autocrat who fled the country is providing funds for this. ... With whose help? There are several parties spreading misinformation in the country. They tried to sell various tickets to the people before the election. These two sides have joined hands. One is providing money from across the border, while the other is sitting here and trying to create instability.”

Tarique Rahman said the Bangladesh Nationalist Party (BNP) government was working to bring stability to the country, strengthen security, reopen closed industrial establishments and make farmers self-reliant. The government was also trying to improve workers’ skills and create employment opportunities at home and abroad. However, he alleged, several political parties were trying to disrupt these efforts by creating disorder on the streets.

The prime minister said conspiracies had also been hatched in the past when initiatives were taken to develop the country under the leadership of martyred President Ziaur Rahman and former Prime Minister Khaleda Zia. He alleged that attempts were still being made to obstruct the country's progress.

BNP embraces the Liberation War and July uprising

BNP Chairman and Prime Minister Tarique Rahman said at the rally that the party embraces both the Liberation War and the July mass uprising of 2024.

He said hundreds of students and general people had been killed before the autocratic regime fell during the 2024 mass uprising. A memorial was inaugurated at Osmani Udyan in Dhaka in memory of those who were killed, he added.

Tarique Rahman said all political parties that claimed to uphold the July uprising had been invited to the inauguration ceremony. However, representatives of several parties did not attend.

In an apparent reference to Jamaat-e-Islami, he said, “Just as they deceived the people in 1971, we have seen them deceive the July movement of 2024 as well. They say one thing, but their actions reflect something else.”

Referring to declining water levels in the Padma River in the Rajshahi region, the prime minister said the BNP government had plans to build barrages on the Padma and Teesta rivers to address water shortages.

He said the government would hold discussions with the relevant parties to secure Bangladesh’s fair share of water. If necessary, it would go to whatever lengths required to secure the people's right to water, he added.

Earlier, after taking the stage, Prime Minister Tarique Rahman distributed Tk 120 million in incentives to 38,970 sugarcane farmers in the Rajshahi region through mobile financial services in a single transaction.

The rally was chaired by BNP Senior Joint Secretary General Ruhul Kabir Rizvi and moderated by Md Mahfuzur Rahman, general secretary of Rajshahi city BNP and administrator of the city corporation. Among others, Land Minister Md Mizanur Rahman Minu, Cultural Affairs Minister Nitai Roy Chowdhury and BNP Standing Committee member Gayeshwar Chandra Roy addressed the rally.

‘We want to change the politics of the past’

Earlier, at around noon, Prime Minister Tarique Rahman visited the Dharmasabha Radha Gobinda Temple in Rangpur city.

“We want to change the kind of politics we have seen in the past. The people are the main force behind this change. Like before, the present government wants to move forward with the people by its side,” he said.

The prime minister said people wanted stability and security in the country. “Sadly, we have been seeing for some time that while the present government is trying to build unity and move forward with everyone, a certain group is trying to spread various misinformation about these efforts,” he said.

Tarique Rahman said the people had elected the current government. While the BNP had won seats in some regions but not in others, he said, the government wanted to represent everyone.

“The present government wants to be a government for those who voted for us as well as those who did not. We want to work for everyone,” he said.

The prime minister said Tk 18 billion had been allocated two weeks earlier for the development of Rangpur city. In addition, the government would use district councils under the local government system to build bridges and culverts in villages, upazilas and unions according to local needs.

Temple authorities welcomed the prime minister upon his arrival. He took selfies with children and toured the puja mandap. He also handed over a cheque for Tk 1 million for the temple’s development.

The prime minister said he had instructed the Ministry of Public Administration to complete construction of facilities behind the temple to accommodate worshippers travelling from distant areas.

After visiting the temple, Tarique Rahman left for Rajshahi. The military aircraft carrying him landed at Shah Makhdum Airport in Rajshahi at around 3:00 pm. He arrived at the rally venue at Madrasa Ground half an hour later.

item.title: PM’s Japan visit: Reducing metro rail costs, loan interest rates likely to be discussed
item.description:
Reducing metro rail costs and interest rates on loans taken from Japan will be among the issues discussed during Prime Minister Tarique Rahman's four-day visit to Japan.

Foreign Secretary Asad Alam Siam disclosed this at a press conference organised by the Ministry of Foreign Affairs on Tuesday afternoon ahead of the prime minister's upcoming visit to Japan.

The foreign secretary said several memorandums of understanding (MoUs) could be signed during the visit on issues including cooperation in agriculture, fisheries, human resource development and skills enhancement, civil aviation, marine environmental conservation and modernisation of local government.

Asked how many MoUs would be signed, Asad Alam Siam said, "We are discussing around eight MoUs. We hope three to four of them will be signed."

Several MoUs likely to be announced during PM's visit to Japan

The cost of Dhaka's MRT Line-1 has increased by 83 per cent, while that of MRT Line 5 has risen by 113 per cent. Asked whether these issues and a reduction in interest rates on loans from Japan would be discussed, the foreign secretary said, "We have sought various forms of technical assistance from Japan for infrastructure development, including what you mentioned – capital funding and substantial technical support. These infrastructure cooperation issues will certainly come up during the bilateral meeting between the two prime ministers. Besides the metro rail, there are other areas of mutual cooperation in infrastructure development. So, these matters will be discussed in detail."

Asad Alam Siam said, "We want to obtain loans at lower interest rates from all countries. However, there are global arrangements as well as domestic factors specific to each country. These are very important. The issues you have raised will be discussed. The outcome will be clear after the discussions."

Referring to the current relations between Bangladesh and Japan as being at the level of a "strategic partnership", the foreign secretary said various joint cooperation initiatives were underway in areas including Bangladesh's infrastructure development, technological advancement, human resource development and security cooperation.

He hoped that the visit would further strengthen these activities.

The foreign secretary said the prime minister's upcoming visit would create an opportunity to make relations between the two countries "deeper and stronger".

He noted that the signing of the Economic Partnership Agreement (EPA) between Bangladesh and Japan in February had opened up new opportunities to expand trade and investment.

As one of Bangladesh's major development partners, Japan has been supporting the construction and implementation of several important infrastructure and connectivity projects, including the metro rail, the third terminal of Hazrat Shahjalal International Airport and the Matarbari deep-sea port.

The foreign secretary said the prime minister's visit would create opportunities to expand access for Bangladeshi products to the Japanese market, increase Japanese investment and strengthen business ties. It would also pave the way for broader cooperation in new areas, including renewable energy, the environment, science, technology, digital innovation, research and human resource development.

He said Prime Minister Tarique Rahman would hold a bilateral meeting with Japanese Prime Minister Sanae Takaichi at her office on 26 October, the second day of his visit. He would also attend a dinner hosted by the Japanese prime minister in his honour.

In addition, the prime minister will hold courtesy meetings with representatives of the Japan-Bangladesh Parliamentary Friendship League, the chairman of the Japan-Bangladesh Committee for Commercial and Economic Cooperation, the president of the Japan International Cooperation Agency (JICA), the governor of the Japan Bank for International Cooperation (JBIC), the president of the Japan External Trade Organization (JETRO) and the chairman of the Sasakawa Peace Foundation.

The foreign secretary also said Prime Minister Tarique Rahman would deliver the keynote address at the Japan-Bangladesh Economic Forum.

Asad Alam Siam said the prime minister's visit would help accelerate the implementation of ongoing priority projects with Japan and ensure their timely completion. It would also strengthen the economic partnership, increase economic and development assistance, and ensure the continuation of security cooperation.

Prime Minister Tarique Rahman will leave for Japan on 26 October on a four-day visit.

Sources said, his entourage will include his wife, Zubaida Rahman; Finance Minister Amir Khasru Mahmud Chowdhury; Prime Minister's Adviser on Finance and Planning Rashed Al Mahmud Titumir; State Minister for Foreign Affairs Humaiun Kobir; State Minister for Power, Energy and Mineral Resources Aninda Islam Amit; Prime Minister's Adviser on Posts, Telecommunications and Information Technology Rehan Asif Asad; BIDA Chairman Ashik Chowdhury; and Prime Minister's Special Assistant for Overseas Employment in the Asia-Pacific region Md Shakirul Islam Khan.

Officials concerned of the Bangladesh government, media representatives and other distinguished individuals will also accompany the prime minister as part of the delegation.

item.title: What's behind Egypt's move towards possible military involvement in Saudi-Yemen conflict?
item.description:
Egypt's parliament is expected to vote next week on whether to authorise the armed forces to help defend Saudi Arabia against attacks by Yemen's Houthis if Riyadh requests its support.

The move would bring the Arab world's most populous country closer to direct military involvement in the widening conflicts unleashed by the US-Israeli air assault on Iran in February.

President Abdel Fattah al-Sisi requested the approval in a speech on Saturday, saying Egypt would "never, never forget our brothers in the Gulf" and telling Saudi Arabia's leaders that Cairo would "take any measure to protect you".

Like the Gulf states that have come under attack from Tehran in the Iran war, Egypt is a longstanding partner in the US-led security order that is being tested by the conflict.

What is Egypt’s stance on the Iran war?

Sisi's comments marked a clear escalation from the more measured tone authorities have tended to adopt since the Iran war started. Though Egypt has repeatedly voiced strong support for its Gulf allies, Cairo has stopped short of publicly committing itself to a direct combat role in the conflict.

In May, the presence of Egyptian Rafale fighter jets in the United Arab Emirates was disclosed in Emirati state media coverage of an official visit by Sisi. Egyptian coverage of the visit did not mention the deployment. When Saudi Arabia signed a joint defence agreement with Turkey and Pakistan in August, Egypt did not join, though it said it was considering it.

The tone started to shift after the Houthis stepped up attacks on Saudi oil and other infrastructure. Saudi Arabia’s Crown Prince Mohammed bin Salman last month visited Egypt, where he discussed the need to ensure freedom and security of navigation in the Bab el-Mandeb Strait and the Red Sea, on which both countries have long coastlines.

What’s at stake for Egypt?

Egypt's economic stability has long been tied up with the oil-producing Gulf. Remittances from Egyptian expatriate workers there are an important source of foreign currency and income for families back home at a time of double-digit inflation worsened by surging food and fuel prices.

Saudi Arabia, the UAE and other Gulf countries have been among Sisi's key financial backers, providing tens of billions of dollars of aid, central bank deposits and investments since the army overthrew President Mohamed Morsi, a senior Muslim Brotherhood figure, in 2013.

"We can never forget how our brothers in the Gulf states stood by Egypt during that period," Sisi said in his speech.

Saudi Arabia has a USD 5.3 billion deposit at Egypt's central bank due this month along with USD 267 million in interest, central bank data shows.

What about security?

Growing security concerns have also pushed Cairo towards a more active stance, analysts say. A drone strike on two gas vessels at the Mediterranean port city of Damietta in July underscored that Egypt could not expect to keep itself fully isolated from the conflict.

"I think they realise that they can't be on the sidelines about this indefinitely," said HA Hellyer, a scholar at the Royal United Services Institute think tank.

For the authorities, the economic and security concerns were "one and the same," he said.

Saudi Arabia and Egypt also have a shared interest in securing shipping through the Red Sea, an outlet for Saudi oil blocked from leaving the Strait of Hormuz. Egypt earns billions of dollars a year from fees on Suez Canal traffic. These overlapping concerns mean "Saudi Arabia's security constitutes a dimension of Egyptian national security," said Sherif Aref, an Egyptian political researcher and journalist.

What sort of military does Egypt bring to the table?

Egypt has one of the Arab world's largest armed forces, with hundreds of thousands of active personnel and large air, land and naval inventories, according to military analysts. Egypt sources equipment from a range of countries, and its air force operates US-made F-16s, French Rafales and Russian-made MiG-29s.

Egypt receives about USD 1.3 billion a year in US military aid, which helps fund its purchases of American military equipment. Washington waived human rights conditions on a tranche of the funds this year after what it called Cairo's "helpful role" since the Iran war began.

In the years after the 2011 uprising that ousted President Hosni Mubarak, the armed forces fought a counterinsurgency campaign against Islamist militants in the Sinai Peninsula. Egypt also contributed air and naval forces to the Saudi-led coalition that intervened in Yemen in 2015, and conducted airstrikes against Islamic State targets in Libya during that country’s civil war.

Egypt has not undertaken a large-scale foreign ground deployment since the 1991 Gulf War, when its troops joined the US-led coalition to drive Iraqi forces from Kuwait. Nearly three decades earlier, President Gamal Abdel Nasser had sent Egyptian forces into Yemen in a costly intervention later compared to the US involvement in the Vietnam War.

What sort of support is likely?

Sisi's speech and subsequent statements have not specified what sort of military forces, if any, Egypt would ultimately intend to send. A deployment of Egyptian troops inside Yemen itself is unlikely, military analysts say.

More likely interventions might include air defence and naval support, said Samir Ragheb, a retired Egyptian military officer who heads the Arab Foundation for Development and Strategic Studies think tank.

"The threats, missiles and drones, require air defence and air forces," he said, adding that the navy could be used for protecting ships, naval operations against piracy and protecting the Saudi coastline.

Still, the entry of another large conventional Arab military would not "suddenly solve the Houthi problem", said Andreas Krieg, senior security studies lecturer at King's ​College London.

"The Houthis are difficult precisely because they generate disproportionate effect through missiles, drones, dispersed forces and geography. Egypt cannot bomb that problem away," he said.

"What Cairo can do is strengthen Saudi resilience, improve Red Sea control, share the defensive burden and increase the political cost of continued attacks."

item.title: Bangladesh seeks Portuguese mission in Dhaka, direct air connectivity
item.description:
Bangladesh has called for the establishment of a resident Portuguese diplomatic mission in Dhaka and expressed interest in introducing direct air connectivity between the two countries to strengthen bilateral relations.

Bangladesh Ambassador to Portugal SM Kamrul Hassan made the proposals during a meeting with Portuguese President António José Seguro at Belém Palace in Lisbon on Monday, according to a press release issued by the Bangladesh Embassy in Lisbon.

The ambassador presented his Letters of Credence to the Portuguese president, formally assuming his responsibilities as Bangladesh’s ambassador to Portugal.

The presentation of credentials marks a significant milestone in Bangladesh-Portugal relations and reaffirms Bangladesh’s commitment to further strengthening its longstanding friendship with Portugal and expanding cooperation in areas of mutual interest.

During his call on with the Portuguese President, Ambassador Kamrul conveyed the goodwill and warm greetings of the President of the Republic and the Head of the Government of Bangladesh.

He underscored the importance of establishing a resident Portuguese diplomatic mission in Dhaka, noting that such a step would facilitate closer diplomatic engagement, strengthen institutional ties and expand bilateral cooperation.

He also highlighted the need to operationalise and advance cooperation under a bilateral mobility framework, promote regular and orderly migration, and reducing the existing trade deficit.

Highlighting the importance of people to people connectivity the Ambassador expressed interest in establishing direct air connectivity.

The Portuguese President acknowledged and appreciated the contribution of the Bangladeshi community in Portugal and emphasised the importance of their integration into Portuguese society.

The discussions also highlighted opportunities to deepen cooperation in trade and investment, maritime affairs, renewable energy, ICT and people-to-people exchanges.

The Embassy of Bangladesh in Lisbon remains committed to advancing the shared interests of the two countries, strengthening economic and institutional ties, and translating the longstanding friendship into tangible outcomes for the mutual benefit of both peoples.

item.title: ‘Ice Cream’ on Chorki: Razz and Tushi look back on their first film
item.description:
Sariful Razz and Nazifa Tushi made their film debuts with ‘Ice Cream’. Directed by Redoan Rony, the film was released in cinemas on 29 April 2016. A decade later, their debut film has arrived on OTT platform Chorki. Ice Cream has been available on the platform since midnight on Monday.

On 16 October, Chorki’s verified Facebook page published the film’s thematic poster. The following day, Sunday, it announced the release date, writing, “The temperature is rising, and the ice of anticipation is melting! In just two days, we’ll find out who melts and who freezes! Redoan Rony’s Chorki-exclusive film Ice Cream arrives on 20 October.”

The rise and rise of Nazifa Tushi

The announcement sparked discussion among viewers. When Rony shared the poster, the comments reflected both their eagerness to watch the film and their fond memories of it.

The feelings of the film’s director and three actors echoed those of the audience. Ahead of its OTT release, they looked back on the excitement of making their first film, their experiences on set, their friendship and their dream of creating a film featuring a host of new faces.

For Sariful Razz, Ice Cream laid the foundation of his acting career. “There must be some differences between the Razz of 10 years ago and the Razz of today. But Ice Cream is the foundation of my life that helped me reach where I am today,” the actor said.

For Nazifa Tushi, Ice Cream was not only her first film but also her first job in the entertainment industry. She went straight into cinema without having acted in television dramas or advertisements. Looking back on the experience, she is amazed by how it all happened.

“I stepped onto the canvas of cinema without understanding or knowing that it was such a vast canvas. Back then, I knew nothing about the industry and did not understand how it worked. I simply had a desire to act. From that perspective, I was young and thought I could do a film,” Tushi said.

She learnt a great deal while working on her debut film. The actor, who also starred in Hawa, said, “I understood many things after making Ice Cream. It feels good that audiences will be able to watch the film again.”

What's eating Shariful Razz?

“I said back then that everyone should watch it, even if only once, and I am saying the same thing now. But it is truly amazing to think about how we made the film and that 10 years have already passed,” she added.

Ice Cream was Redoan Rony’s second feature film. He directed it and also wrote its story, screenplay and dialogue. He said the decision to cast newcomers was driven by the demands of the story. As the film reaches audiences again after a decade, the director has also been reminded of the dreams and hard work that went into its making.

Reflecting on the film’s arrival on Chorki, Rony said, “Ten years ago, when we made Ice Cream, it was driven by the tireless efforts and fresh dreams of a group of young people, a host of new faces and boundless emotion.”

“Although the equations of life change with time, some feelings and realities never fade. As the film returns to Chorki’s screen, I feel that its subject matter remains highly relevant. It is as if that old dream is returning in a new form,” he added.

The director is also delighted that the film can now reach audiences both at home and abroad. He said those who missed it in cinemas or were living outside the country can now watch Ice Cream on Chorki from anywhere in Bangladesh or around the world.

The film’s songs may also bring back memories for old-time viewers and listeners. Songs including Boka Chand and Poth feature vocals by Arnob, Armeen Musa, Sharmin Sultana Sumi and Minar Rahman.

Alongside Razz, Tushi and Uday, the cast includes ATM Shamsuzzaman, Diti, Omar Sani, Sayem Sadat and Nadia Khanam.

item.title: Sweety spoke to father in Bangladesh before execution in Saudi Arabia
item.description:
Sweety Akter married while she was in Class Eight, but the marriage did not last. After separating from her husband, she returned to her parents’ home with her child. Later, under pressure from her family, she married again. But after her second husband moved to Saudi Arabia, he cut off contact with her. She was at a loss about what to do.

Thinking about her daughter’s future and hoping to ease her parents’ financial hardship, Sweety Akter went to Saudi Arabia three years ago. She worked there as a cleaner. But just six months after arriving in the country, she was arrested.

Sweety had told her family that several women working with her in Saudi Arabia had illegally purchased a car and that she had been arrested along with them in connection with the incident.

Although she was in prison, she remained in contact with her parents. She had told them not to worry even if she could not call for some reason. She last spoke to her father on the evening of 13 October, Tuesday. Two days later, her parents learned that her death sentence had been carried out.

Two Bangladeshi nationals were recently executed in Saudi Arabia after being convicted of committing immoral acts at a mosque in the holy city of Mecca. The Saudi Press Agency (SPA) confirmed the executions on 14 October, Wednesday, citing the country’s Ministry of Interior. The two executed Bangladeshis were Nazrul Islam and Sweety Akter.

After son’s execution in Saudi Arabia, parents want to see his body just once

Mirzapur Upazila Nirbahi Officer (UNO) Zahurul Alam told Prothom Alo that they had learned about the execution of the two Bangladeshi nationals in Saudi Arabia.

‘Bring her body home’

Sweety Akter was from a village in Mirzapur upazila of Tangail. She was the daughter of Md Fazal Mia and Johura Begum and the youngest of five sisters.

Visiting Sweety’s home at around 9am on Tuesday, this correspondent found several people gathered in the courtyard, talking among themselves. Some were her relatives, while others were neighbours. Her parents were sitting on the veranda.

As soon as Johura Begum was asked about her daughter, she began to cry. Composing herself with difficulty, she said, “How will I survive? Bring my Sweety back to me.”

Md Fazal Mia, Sweety Akter’s fatherShe went to Saudi Arabia through an agency in March 2023 and worked there as a cleaner. For about six months after she went to Saudi Arabia, we spoke to her regularly. Then, one day, she suddenly called and told us she was in prison

Johura Begum was unable to speak properly because of her tears. At one point, she said, “My daughter, you suffered so much, yet you didn’t tell anyone. You didn’t even tell me… Bring my daughter’s body home. I want to see her.”

Sweety Akter’s father, Md Fazal Mia, then spoke about his daughter.

“She went to Saudi Arabia through an agency in March 2023 and worked there as a cleaner. For about six months after she went to Saudi Arabia, we spoke to her regularly. Then, one day, she suddenly called and told us she was in prison. Apparently, some of her friends had illegally bought a car, and she was arrested along with the others over the incident.

Saudi Arabia executes 2 Bangladeshis for indecent acts inside Mecca mosque

“While she was in prison, we sometimes spoke after a week and sometimes after a month. This continued for a year, and then contact suddenly stopped.”

Fazal Mia said Sweety contacted them by phone again after a year. She told them she was still in prison and asked them not to worry if she could not call.

“This continued for about four months. After that, we had no further contact. I last spoke to Sweety on Tuesday (13 October), after Maghrib prayers. But she did not tell me anything about a trial or a death sentence.”

‘We do not believe the allegations’

Sweety’s relatives believe she may have fallen victim to a conspiracy by someone in Saudi Arabia. None of her family members believes the allegations brought against her.

Sweetie later went to Saudi Arabia in search of a better life, leaving her daughter with one of her sisters. The girl, now nine, studies in Class three at a local primary school.

Sweety’s cousin Salma Akter, who is older than her, was present while her parents spoke about her. Salma said Sweetie had never been fortunate enough to have a stable married life.

After Sweetie’s second marriage, the family borrowed money to send her husband to Saudi Arabia. But he cut off contact after arriving there.

Sweetie later went to Saudi Arabia in search of a better life, leaving her daughter with one of her sisters. The girl, now nine, studies in Class three at a local primary school.

Salma repeatedly broke down in tears while speaking. When she eventually regained some composure, she said Sweety could never have committed any wrongdoing.

She then said, “My uncle works hard, digging the earth to earn his living. Ours is a family struggling with poverty. She went abroad because her parents were poor. There are five daughters, and my uncle has no son. If we had known this would happen to her, would we ever have allowed her to go abroad?”

item.title: 7,500 cancer patients await radiotherapy as appointments stretch to 2028
item.description:
Mohammad Mostafa Kamal travelled from Gopalganj to the National Institute of Cancer Research and Hospital (NICRH) in Dhaka for radiotherapy after undergoing surgery for an abdominal tumour and completing chemotherapy.
He arrived at the hospital on the morning of Monday to seek an appointment, only to learn that the radiotherapy department was no longer accepting new registrations.
“My doctor told me I would need radiotherapy after chemotherapy, but I cannot get an appointment. We are poor people and cannot afford treatment at a private hospital. I travelled all the way from Gopalganj to receive treatment at a government facility, but I still cannot get a slot,” he said.
Sathia Khatun, who travelled from Tangail after undergoing surgery for breast cancer, faced the same problem.
“The doctors told me they were not accepting new registrations. I cannot afford a private hospital, so I have to rely on government treatment. We live hand to mouth,” she said.
“The hospital told me I would have to wait two years because the machines are out of order. I did not even know radiotherapy was unavailable here. I travelled all the way from my village, but I cannot get treatment,” she added.
Like Kamal and Sathia, thousands of cancer patients are facing prolonged waits for radiotherapy at the country's premier public cancer hospital.
According to the World Health Organization (WHO), more than half of all cancer patients worldwide may require radiotherapy at some stage of their treatment. The organisation has stressed the need to expand access while ensuring safe, quality care.
Hospital sources said four of NICRH's six radiotherapy machines had been out of service for more than two years.
The remaining two are handling the hospital's patient load, with more than 7,000 people waiting for treatment. Some patients have appointments scheduled for the end of 2028.
New registrations have been suspended for the past month and a half because the hospital can no longer accommodate additional patients, authorities said.
Doctors said radiotherapy often needs to begin promptly after cancer surgery, depending on the patient's condition and treatment plan. Delays can raise concerns about cancer recurrence or its spread to other parts of the body.
During a visit to the hospital, this correspondent found the two functioning machines being used to treat existing patients and those already on the waiting list. Staff said the machines were operating beyond their intended capacity.
Doctors said an average of 250–300 patients receive treatment daily in three shifts, from 8am to midnight.
NICRH Director Professor Dr Mostafa Aziz Sumon told Dhaka Tribune that new registrations had been stopped because existing appointments were already scheduled through the end of 2028.
“It is not acceptable for cancer patients to wait two years for treatment. Around 7,500 patients are waiting for appointments. We are providing as much treatment as possible using our two functioning machines,” he said.
Photo: Dhaka Tribune
He expressed hope that new machines would arrive by mid-2027, allowing the hospital to treat more patients and reduce waiting times.
Cancer treatment is often prolonged and expensive, leaving many middle- and low-income families unable to afford private healthcare. As a result, patients from across the country depend on NICRH for comparatively affordable treatment.
Doctors at the hospital said a course of radiotherapy generally takes four to eight weeks to complete. Although new patients were previously registered alongside those already receiving treatment, the growing patient load has forced the hospital to suspend registrations temporarily.
Experts said a single specialised hospital could not handle the treatment needs of the country's large cancer patient population. They called for expanded cancer care at divisional and district levels, alongside adequate equipment and trained personnel.
They also stressed that purchasing radiotherapy machines alone would not be enough. The country needs more trained radiation oncologists, medical physicists and radiation therapists to ensure access to modern cancer treatment.
Public health and vaccinologist Tajul Islam A Bari described the prolonged wait for radiotherapy at a government hospital as deeply distressing for patients with a life-threatening disease.
“Delays in treatment increase risks to patients' lives. Questions are also being raised about why the government did not arrange the necessary machines earlier to address the crisis,” he said.
He called for urgent alternative arrangements, including coordination with private hospitals, to ensure patients could receive treatment without further delays.
According to 2024 estimates from GLOBOCAN, compiled by the International Agency for Research on Cancer (IARC) under the WHO, approximately 187,263 people were newly diagnosed with cancer in Bangladesh in 2024. Of them, 107,820 were men and 79,443 were women.
A large proportion receive treatment at public and private hospitals, while some travel abroad for care. The relatively low cost of treatment at NICRH contributes to its heavy patient load.
Health Minister Sardar Sakhawat Husain said the number of cancer patients in Bangladesh was rising at an alarming rate. The government was working to make cancer treatment more accessible and decentralised so patients would not have to wait six to eight months for radiotherapy, he said.
As part of the initiative, 17 new linear accelerators will be installed at government hospitals by June 2027. Six will go to specialised hospitals and medical colleges in Dhaka, while the remaining 11 will be installed at government hospitals outside the capital.
The expansion is expected to give patients outside Dhaka access to modern cancer treatment closer to home and at lower costs.
The minister said the government would not tolerate bureaucratic delays in installing new equipment or removing old, non-functional machines. Measures would also be taken to facilitate the swift import of life-saving cancer treatment equipment, including exemptions from customs duties.

item.title: PM urges cooperation to counter confusion over Liberation War, July uprising
item.description:
Prime Minister Tarique Rahman has called for cooperation among all sections of society to counter attempts to create confusion over Bangladesh’s Liberation War and the 2024 mass uprising, accusing a group of first making the Liberation War controversial and now casting doubt on the uprising.
He made the remarks on Tuesday afternoon while visiting the Dharma Sabha Radha Gobinda Temple on Station Road in Rangpur city and exchanging views with members of the Sanatan community on the occasion of Durga Puja.
Referring to Jamaat-e-Islami, the prime minister said: “Come to parliament and speak. We want to hear your views. If you say anything in the interests of the people, we are willing to accept it.”
Tarique Rahman said the government was working to improve healthcare, business and commerce, and law and order while maintaining stability.
“We want to move beyond all kinds of confusion. For this, I want to be closer to the people of the country and seek their cooperation. We want to work together with people of all religions,” he said.
He added that the government was working to improve healthcare and education, create employment opportunities, support business and commerce, and maintain peace and order. He called on people to cooperate in building a safe Bangladesh.
Tarique Rahman said people of all religions, including Hindus, Muslims, Buddhists and Christians, had participated in the 1971 Liberation War.
“Through our united participation in the war, we liberated the country,” he said.
He also said people from all religious and ethnic backgrounds had taken to the streets during the mass uprising 2 years ago, helping free the country from authoritarian rule.
“We now want to establish a peaceful Bangladesh for the future,” he said.
The prime minister said his party had come to power with a strong public mandate in the recent election. Although the party had won in some regions and lost in others, he said the government considered itself elected by people across the country.
He said the government wanted to ensure balanced development across all regions.
The government had allocated Tk 1,800 crore for Rangpur city’s development at a meeting of the Executive Committee of the National Economic Council (Ecnec), he said. He added that he had instructed the authorities to allocate funds through the district council for infrastructure and road development in Rangpur district and its upazilas.
Earlier, Tarique Rahman arrived at the Radha Gobinda Temple at 12:07pm. Thousands of men and women stood along both sides of the 40km road from Saidpur Airport to the venue to welcome him.
During the event, the prime minister handed over a cheque for Tk 10 lakh to support the temple’s development. He also assured the community of assistance in constructing a 6-story building at the temple for poor and meritorious Sanatan students.
The program was chaired by temple committee president Bhabatosh Sarkar.
Bangladesh Nationalist Party (BNP) Standing Committee member Goyasawar Chandra Roy addressed the event, along with Cultural Affairs Minister Nitai Roy Chowdhury, Dhaka district BNP president Nipun Roy Chowdhury, State Minister for Local Government Mir Shahe Alam and other leaders.
